questions.question: In which nephron segment does PTH promote urinary phosphate excretion?
options: Collecting ducts
Proximal tubules
Loop of Henle
Distal convoluted tubules

questions.question: What is the normal physiological range of plasma calcium maintained by PTH?
Which hormone directly blocks the bone-resorbing action of parathormone (PTH)?
options: Aldosterone
Calcitonin
Adrenaline
Thyroxine

questions.question: A patient's parathyroid gland remains fully functional despite surgical removal of the hypothalamus, as PTH secretion is independent of the CNS. Which factor normally regulates PTH secretion?
options: Plasma sodium concentration through positive feedback
Plasma calcium concentration via metabolic negative feedback
Hypothalamic releasing hormones via neural pathways
ANS innervation supplying direct stimulatory input
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B. Plasma calcium concentration via metabolic negative feedback

questions.question: A patient with severe hypocalcemia is found to have reduced calcium reabsorption in the distal renal tubules. What is the normal renal action of PTH?
options: Increase phosphate reabsorption in proximal tubules
Decrease activation of vitamin D hydroxylase enzyme
Increase calcium reabsorption in distal tubules and collecting ducts
Decrease urinary excretion of phosphate in proximal tubules
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C. Increase calcium reabsorption in distal tubules and collecting ducts

questions.question: Cortisol causes which of the following effects on electrolytes?
options: Increased Na⁺ excretion
Increased K⁺ retention
Na⁺ and water retention
Strong K⁺ excretion under normal conditions
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C. Na⁺ and water retention

questions.question: A 58-year-old woman with chronic heart failure shows elevated atrial pressure, leading to increased release of atrial natriuretic factor (ANF). Which effect of ANF helps regulate aldosterone secretion in this condition?
options: Stimulating renin secretion to raise aldosterone levels
Enhancing zona glomerulosa responsiveness to angiotensin II
Inhibiting aldosterone and renin secretion through negative feedback
Increasing aldosterone secretion during high blood volume
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C. Inhibiting aldosterone and renin secretion through negative feedback

questions.question: A man presents with increased blood volume and higher arterial pressure. Physical examination shows reduced salivary sodium content and increased intestinal sodium absorption. Which general action of aldosterone explains these findings?
options: Increasing sodium loss in sweat and saliva
Increasing sodium absorption in sweat glands, salivary glands, and GIT
Decreasing water absorption from the gastrointestinal tract
Reducing sodium reabsorption in renal collecting ducts
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B. Increasing sodium absorption in sweat glands, salivary glands, and GIT
